novel_features.name: Cold-start observatory
novel_features.description: See how often your functions cold-start and how slow those starts are, with the projected cost of moving to a Premium always-ready plan.
novel_features.rationale: Cold start is not a first-class Azure metric; it must be derived from Application Insights request gaps and new role-instance appearances over local time-series history that a stateless az call never accumulates.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to answer 'are cold starts hurting us, and is Premium worth it' instead of guessing from anecdotes.

novel_features.name: Scaling & exec-drift trend
novel_features.description: Track instance scale-out and execution-time drift for an app over a time window, flagging when p95 duration creeps above baseline.
novel_features.rationale: Requires persisted per-window history of invocations and instances that no single ARM or App Insights call returns at once.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to catch a slow-degrading function before it pages you.

novel_features.name: Plan-fit recommendation
novel_features.description: Per-app recommendation of Consumption vs Premium vs Dedicated across a resource group, based on invocation density, cold-start sensitivity, and duration.
novel_features.rationale: Joins hosting-plan tier, invocation history, and cold-start derivation across every app in a group — a multi-source correlation impossible in one stateless call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when deciding how to host a fleet of functions cost-effectively.

novel_features.name: Config-drift detector
novel_features.description: Diff app settings across function apps and their deployment slots, flagging settings present in one environment but not another and plaintext values that should be Key Vault references.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-app and cross-slot comparison plus Key-Vault-reference classification needs the full local settings store, not a per-resource read.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before a release to catch dev/prod config divergence.

novel_features.name: Secret-sprawl audit
novel_features.description: Flag app settings holding raw secret values instead of @Microsoft.KeyVault references, plus stale or unused function keys.
novel_features.rationale: Separating 'secret in plaintext' from 'proper Key Vault reference' and correlating with key usage needs the joined settings+keys store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to find leaked secrets and tighten config hygiene.

novel_features.name: Invocation failure clustering
novel_features.description: Cluster recent invocation failures by function and exception type from Application Insights over a time window.
novel_features.rationale: Clustering across a window of request/exception telemetry needs persisted local invocation history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to triage which function and which exception is failing most.

novel_features.name: Stale-function finder
novel_features.description: Find functions with zero invocations in the last N days as cleanup candidates.
novel_features.rationale: Knowing a function had zero invocations requires persisted invocation history; a live call only sees the present.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to prune dead functions and shrink your attack surface.

narrative.headline: Inspect, audit, and right-size your Azure Functions from the terminal — cold-start trends, config drift, and plan-fit answers the portal and az don't give you.
narrative.value_prop: Azure Functions runs your code on demand without you managing servers. This CLI is a read-only inspector for the Function Apps in your Azure subscription: it lists your apps and functions, reads their settings and keys, and pulls invocation history from Application Insights into a local database. That local history unlocks answers a stateless `az` command can't give — like how often your functions cold-start, whether you should move off the Consumption plan, and where plaintext secrets are hiding in your app settings. It does not deploy code (use `func` or `az functionapp` for that); it tells you what your functions are doing and how to improve them.
narrative.auth_narrative:
This CLI talks to Azure Resource Manager using a standard Azure credential, the same way the official tools do. The simplest setup for a newcomer:

1. Have an Azure subscription with at least one Function App.
2. Create a read-only service principal (run once, in the Azure Cloud Shell or after `az login`):
   `az ad sp create-for-rbac --name azure-functions-admin --role Reader --scopes /subscriptions/<your-subscription-id>`
   That prints an `appId`, `password`, and `tenant`.
3. Export them so the CLI can read them:
   `export AZURE_TENANT_ID=<tenant>`
   `export AZURE_CLIENT_ID=<appId>`
   `export AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=<password>`
   `export AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<your-subscription-id>`
4. Run `azure-functions-admin doctor` to confirm everything connects.

The `Reader` role is enough for every command except `keys`, which lists function/host keys — that needs the `Website Contributor` role (or a custom role granting `Microsoft.Web/sites/host/listkeys/action`). If you are already signed in with `az login`, the CLI will use that session automatically and you can skip the service principal.

quickstart.comment: Confirms the CLI is installed and shows what a health check will verify (no credentials needed).
Lists every Function App in your subscription — your starting inventory.
Pulls apps, functions, settings, and invocation history into the local database so analysis commands work offline and fast.
The headline answer for one app: how often it cold-starts and how slow those starts are (swap in your app name).
Per-app Consumption-vs-Premium-vs-Dedicated recommendation across your whole subscription (add --resource-group to scope it).

troubleshoots.fix: Export AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, and AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, or run `az login` first.
Check AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID is correct and the service principal has Reader granted at the subscription scope, not just one resource group.
Listing keys needs the Website Contributor role: `az role assignment create --assignee <appId> --role 'Website Contributor' --scope /subscriptions/<id>`.

troubleshoots.symptom: coldstart or metrics shows no data
troubleshoots.fix: The app must have Application Insights enabled (an APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING app setting). Without it, there is no invocation telemetry to analyze.
ARM throttles reads per subscription; the CLI backs off and retries automatically — re-run after a moment or narrow the resource group.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you need to understand or audit Azure Functions you already run: take inventory across a subscription, decide whether to move an app off the Consumption plan to kill cold starts, audit app settings for leaked secrets or dev/prod drift, or triage which function is failing. It is the right tool for read-only inspection and analysis, especially for agents and scripts that want JSON output and a local cache.
anti_triggers: Deploying or publishing function code — use `func azure functionapp publish` or `az functionapp deployment`.
Creating, restarting, scaling, or deleting function apps — this CLI is read-only by design.
Changing app settings or rotating keys — use `az functionapp config appsettings set` / `az functionapp keys set`.
Building a new Functions project — use the Azure Functions Core Tools (`func init`).

recipes.title: Cold-start check before a plan decision
recipes.explanation: Returns cold-start frequency, p50/p95 cold-start latency, and the projected always-ready cost so you can decide on Premium with numbers, not vibes.

recipes.title: Audit a whole resource group for plan fit
recipes.explanation: One call ranks every app's ideal plan from its real invocation density and cold-start sensitivity.

recipes.title: Find leaked secrets in app settings
recipes.explanation: Flags settings holding raw secret values that should be @Microsoft.KeyVault references, plus unused keys.

recipes.title: Trim a verbose response for an agent
recipes.explanation: App-list responses are large and deeply nested; --select with dotted paths returns only the fields an agent needs, saving context.

recipes.title: Triage today's failures
recipes.explanation: Clusters the last day of invocation failures by function and exception type so you fix the biggest one first.
